text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Railway tickets to increase up to 52 precent in long-distance travel, as fares change on Januray 1, in line with an international standard of setting prices.
- Medical doctors' and nurses' salaries to go up between 4 and 30 percent, following an agreement signed between the Health Ministry and eight health workers' trade unions.
- Herceg-Bosna will not be scrapped abruptly, but will rather be phased out gradually, says in an interview a member of the Bosnian presidency, Kresimir Zubak.

- In 1997 salaries will be formed without government decrees for the first time: Workers' wages will rise up to 9 percent. Those who are receiving less money at the moment will also enjoy a smaller increase in their pay.

- According to the state statistics bureau retail prices in 1996 had gone up by an average 3.5 percent in a year-on-year comparison with 1995. The prices of goods went up 2.4 percent, while services were up by 8.6 percent compared to 1995. The monthly break down of the rise in retail prices in 1996 amounted to 0.279 percent. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
